text.p: Australian bond spreads continued their narrowing bias against other dollar bloc countries on Friday, as a bullish market strengthened on the back of a strong U.S market and ongoing hopes of a local rate cut.

The spread narrowing has been most pronounced at the long end, with the short end constrained in how far it can rally by the fact that a local rate cut has been well factored into the market, traders said.
However, there was still some potential for the short end to rally, so the narrowing tone could continue next week.
Local 10-year bond spreads ended the week 12 points narrower to U.S. 10-years, and 13 and 21 one points narrower against Canadian and New Zealand bonds respectively.
Three year bonds narrowed by four points to the U.S. over the week, and the outperformance of the long end was reflected in a marked flattening of the local yield curve.
Over the week, both the futures and the physical curves flattened by 13 points. The curve is now at its flattest since the end of May.
